explanation: The wooden prototype ran on two metal wheels set at right angles. Engelbart showed it to the public in 1968, in a demonstration later nicknamed the Mother of All Demos.

claims.text: The first computer mouse, built in 1964 for Douglas Engelbart's team at the Stanford Research Institute, had a wooden case.
The prototype mouse's case was not made of plastic, aluminium or brass.
The prototype mouse rolled on two metal wheels set at right angles to each other.
Engelbart demonstrated the mouse in public on 9 December 1968, in what was later called the Mother of All Demos.
